use_case_name: Monitor Current and Past Auction Status

claims.content: Customer wants to monitor the current and past auction status of a product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.

scope_contract.goal_statement: Customer wants to monitor the current and past auction status of a product item, including its auction status (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed), dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Customer views one product item's current and past auction status records in the Bid History section, seeing status labels, closing date/time (or 'Active' for a live auction), auction sequence numbers, SKU, the customer's last bid, SmartBid if one was placed, and the winning bid.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer begins by choosing to view a product item's auction status/history.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer sees the product item's current and past auction status and the associated bid history details.
in_scope_actions: View current and past auction status for a product item
View auction status categories (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed) with dates/times, bid counts, and winning bidder information
View Bid History details: closing date/time or 'Active', auction sequence numbers, SKU, customer's last bid, SmartBid if placed, and winning bid
excluded_adjacent_actions: Placing, updating, or canceling bids (including QuickBid/SmartBid submission)
Managing auction scheduling or product/SKU administration
Post-auction notifications, offers, or follow-up processes
variant_dimensions: Auction status category displayed (Unscheduled, Scheduled, Current/Live, Closed)
Presence of a customer SmartBid on an auction

claims.content: Customer

The user has an authenticated session in the Auction Admin Application and is in the Auction Admin Main Menu workspace from which auction status monitoring/reporting pages (such as the Current Auctions Status Page and SKU History page) can be accessed.
The target customer history view has been identified using at least one of Customer Email Address, Customer Home Phone, or Customer Name (Last, First).
Customer initiates the auction status view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking “Go.”
The Customer initiates the auction status/history view for a specific product item by entering the Product ID and clicking “Go.”
The system displays the search results in two sections: a top section showing product summary data and a bottom section listing the item's auction history data on separate lines.
The system lists each individual auction record with its Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount, High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

When the user selects 'Bid History', the system displays the Bid History section showing the item's closing date/time (or 'Active' if the auction is still live), auction sequence numbers, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, SmartBid (max bid), and the winning bid; the user also views the Product Details page, which displays the Item Bid History table with bidder Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User status.
Diverges from Step 4: If an auction is still live, the Bid History section displays 'Active' instead of a closing date/time for that auction; if the auction is closed, its closing date/time is shown.
Diverges from Step 2: The page provides a 'Recently Ended Auctions' link; if the customer selects it, the system displays the last 24 hours of auction history as an alternative viewing scope.

If a search results in no matches (No Results Found), the system displays a 'No Results' page which includes a 'Search Tips' section with specific advice: check for typos/misspellings, remove unnecessary words like 'and', 'the', or 'a', try plural and singular forms of the word, use fewer or more generic keywords, and contact support if tips fail.

missing_aspects: Recovery/retry path after the No Results page is presented
Evidence is needed to confirm that this flow specifically occurs when a 'Product ID entry' fails at Step 1, rather than being a general outcome for any failed search.

claims.content: The system displays the specified product item's current and past auction status history in two sections: a top product summary section and a bottom section listing each auction history record on a separate line.

Each auction history record in the bottom section shows Auction Status, Auction Sequence, Start Date/Time, End Date/Time, Reserve Amount (Opening Bid), High Bid, Number of Bids, and Winner / High Bidder.

The Bid History section lists each auction record with its closing date/time (or 'Active' for a live auction), auction sequence number, product ID (SKU), the customer's last bid, the SmartBid if one was placed, and the winning bid (regardless of who placed it).
The Item Bid History section lists, for each bid, the bidder's Name, Amount, Date Placed, and SmartBid User? status.

quality_flags.detail: [trigger_preconditions_coverage] Preconditions assert an authenticated Auctioneer session in the Auction Admin Main Menu, but the Trigger and primary actor are the Customer. Under rule 1, the entry-context precondition must cover the Customer's access/role needed to initiate the trigger; an Auctioneer-session claim does not establish that the Customer can perform the trigger. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The cited cards do not establish that the actor is specifically a Customer with access to the Auction Admin Application; EC-PC-003 identifies the Current Auctions Status Page as available to the business owner.))

inconsistency_hints: Main Flow stops after displaying the two-section auction-history results and per-auction record fields. It never shows the Bid History section (closing date/time or Active, SKU, customer's last bid, SmartBid, winning bid) or the Item Bid History section (bidder Name, Amount, Date Placed, SmartBid User? status) required by postconditions 3 and 4, so those postconditions are unreachable from the described flow.
Main Flow Step 1 refers to the initiating actor as 'User' instead of the declared Primary Actor 'Customer'; no main_flow step explicitly names 'Customer'.

Precondition 1 requires an authenticated Auctioneer session in the Auction Admin Application, but the Trigger and Main Flow are initiated by the Customer. This precondition does not establish an entry context for the stated primary actor; it describes a different actor's session, so the Customer cannot reach the Trigger from the precondition.

Alternative flow claim 1 states 'Diverges from Step 3' but its content (Bid History section displays 'Active' or closing date/time) is exactly the behavior already specified in main_flow Step 4; Step 3 is about the auction record list, so the attachment point is logically unrelated.

Alternative flow claim 2 states 'Diverges from Step 3' but the SmartBid display in the Bid History section is already described in main_flow Step 4; Step 3 does not concern Bid History, so the branch is attached to the wrong step.
